name: Carnitine Palmitoyltransferase II Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for CPT II Deficiency

criteria.description: Recurrent episodes of rhabdomyolysis triggered by prolonged exercise, fasting, or illness
Reduced CPT II enzyme activity in muscle biopsy or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic variants in the CPT2 gene
Elevated serum creatine kinase (CK) during episodes
Abnormal acylcarnitine profile showing elevated long-chain acylcarnitines

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation plus either reduced enzyme activity or pathogenic CPT2 gene variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing and/or enzyme assay combined with clinical features.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent rhabdomyolysis triggered by prolonged exercise or fasting
pathognomonic.notes: Episodes often accompanied by muscle pain and weakness
searchTerms: muscle breakdown triggered by exercise or fasting
repeated muscle damage after prolonged activity
episodes of muscle injury with exercise or no food

pathognomonic.notes: Dark urine due to muscle breakdown products
searchTerms: muscle protein in urine during attacks
myoglobin in urine during muscle breakdown

common.symptomName: Muscle weakness during or after episodes

common.notes: Often reported during or following episodes

common.symptomName: Elevated serum creatine kinase between episodes
searchTerms: high muscle enzyme levels between attacks

occasional.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting during acute episodes
searchTerms: feeling sick with vomiting during attacks

occasional.notes: Due to impaired fatty acid oxidation
searchTerms: drops in blood sugar during fasting
heart rhythm problems during severe episodes

rare.symptomName: Respiratory failure during severe metabolic crisis
rare.notes: Occurs in severe neonatal or infantile forms
More common in severe early-onset disease

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (CK) during episodes
Abnormal acylcarnitine profile with elevated long-chain acylcarnitines
imaging: Muscle MRI may show edema during acute rhabdomyolysis episodes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in CPT2 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Reduced CPT II enzyme activity in muscle biopsy or cultured fibroblasts

distinguishingFeatures: Muscle biopsy shows ragged red fibers

redFlags: Recurrent rhabdomyolysis with risk of acute renal failure
Severe muscle pain and weakness triggered by minimal exertion
Dark urine indicating myoglobinuria during episodes
references: Bonnefont JP, et al. Carnitine palmitoyltransferase II deficiency: clinical and molecular aspects. Mol Genet Metab. 1999.

Spiekerkoetter U, et al. Long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders and their treatment. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2010.
